q: A query filters `WHERE order_date = '2026-03-15'`, but every data file has a min/max `order_date` range covering the whole year. What happens?
o: Data skipping still prunes most files
No file can be skipped, so all files are read
The query fails until you run `ANALYZE TABLE`
Delta reads only the first file
e: A file can be skipped only if the filter value lies outside its range. Clustering narrows the ranges so more files can be skipped.

q: What does `OPTIMIZE` change about the rows of a table?
o: It removes duplicate rows
It deletes rows older than the retention period
Nothing: it rewrites small files into larger ones with the same rows, and commits with `dataChange: false`
It sorts every row by primary key
e: Compaction only changes the file layout. Results stay the same, and the replaced files remain for time travel until VACUUM.

q: A new 300 GB table is filtered mostly by `customer_id` (2 million distinct values) and `event_date`. Which layout is best?
o: `PARTITIONED BY (customer_id)`
`PARTITIONED BY (event_date)` plus nightly `ZORDER BY (customer_id)`
No layout at all; rely on optimized writes
`CLUSTER BY (customer_id, event_date)`
e: Liquid clustering handles high-cardinality keys and is incremental. Partitioning by customer creates millions of tiny files, and a table under ~1 TB should usually not be partitioned.

q: You run `ALTER TABLE t CLUSTER BY (order_date)` on a liquid clustered table that was clustered by `customer_id`. What happens to the existing files?
o: Nothing right away; new keys apply to future clustering, and `OPTIMIZE t FULL` reclusters old data
They are all rewritten immediately
The command fails because keys cannot be changed
The old files are deleted
e: Changing liquid clustering keys is a metadata-only commit. Existing data is reclustered only when you run `OPTIMIZE ... FULL`.

q: Which statement about predictive optimization is correct?
o: It works on every table, including external tables
It runs `OPTIMIZE`, `VACUUM` and `ANALYZE` automatically for Unity Catalog managed tables
It replaces the transaction log with a faster index
It must be scheduled as a Lakeflow Job
e: Predictive optimization decides when maintenance pays off and runs it for managed tables. External tables still need your own maintenance.
